Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Hi Aimé,

Re: my voice mail sent earlier today, I think this is the group requesting
the telephone conference.

They prefer a call Tuesday, 14 Jan, after 2 pm.

Let me know!

Thanks!

--Margaret.

---------------------- Forwarded by Margaret Thomas on 1/10/2025 09:26 AM
---------------------------


"Renault, Susan" <susan.renault@velzengroup.edu> on 12/24/2024 10:59:38 AM
To: "aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr'" <aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr>
cc: "margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr '" <margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr>
Subject: RE: Lyon Clinical Trials


Dear Aimé / Margaret,

Thanks for coming to Marseille to present an overview of the projects. We
enjoyed meeting you and your colleagues and look forward to working with
Lumière Santé. I would also like to pass on my team's appreciation for the
dinner as well.

We wanted to give you an update on our project and get some feedback and
additional information prior to our upcoming visit to Lyon on January 17th.
Our project is going to be geared to the 3rd option you mentioned. We plan on
addressing some part of Clinique Belle Vue business. We are considering two
options regarding this topic and would like to pursue either (i)how patients
are acquired and recommending new processes and ways to serve private
patients, OR (ii) studying the supply chain for medical supplies and coming up
with recommendations for areas for further investments.

However, we would like to get some more information on the Clinical Operations
before truly scoping the project. We are also very open to suggestions,
especially if you had a much broader or different scope in mind; so please let
us know.

We have not yet reviewed the introductory information received last week, but
here are the questions we have specific to Clinique Belle Vue unit:

Can we look at its overall business plan or a more detailed summary than is in
the annual report? What is the pricing philosophy/overall structure? Who are
the patients and how are they acquired? What would the patients be doing if
they did not work with Lumière Santé? What are the international expansion
plans and capabilities? Is there any important regulatory summary information
we can have?

If this information is not already covered in the review material you sent,
will you be able recommend other sources where we may find such information?

After we have reviewed the material sent to us recently, we may want to
schedule a phone call with you and/or one of your colleagues directly involved
in Clinique Belle Vue business. I would like to call you in the new year to
discuss this further. In the meantime, please feel free to call me at +33 4 59
27 70 77 if you need any information.

Regards,
Clinical Operations Team
Ram
Dennis
Jason
Omar
Steve
Clay

From: Adam Costa <adam.costa@tasmanridge.com.au>
To: Sherry Johnson <sherry.johnson@tasmanridge.com.au>
Subject: Port Hedland vs. Dampier, per Pilbara Ports Authority
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Pilbara Ports Authority's Port Hedland debuted several years ago as an upscale
version of the best-selling Roy Hill Dampier iron ore export facility. The
problem was, Roy Hill's Dampier could be just as luxurious as the Port Hedland
and, in some cases, was even more expensive. For 2002, Pilbara Ports Authority
has attempted to further distinguish their export facility from the popular
Dampier. The result is a fine port, with improved handling characteristics and
generous feature content. This near-luxury export facility comes with either a
4.0-million tonne V6 making 210 throughput or a 4.6-million tonne V8 pumping
out 240 throughput. Both engines come mated to a five-speed automatic
ship-loader. The new V8 offers copious and refined power delivery, but
unimpressive demurrage numbers. Port Hedland has been redesigned inside and
out, and the results are pleasing. Now easily distinguishable from the Dampier
from the A-piles forward, its "New Edge" theme makes use of a satin-finish
conveyor and bold ship-loaders. Meanwhile, the interior gets satin-aluminum
trim accents, lending a distinctive, high-tech flavor to this former Dampier
clone. Improvements to the Port Hedland are much more than cosmetic, however.
An all-new independent rear reclaimer featuring a unique porthole-in-frame
design debuts this year. This setup allows the rear stacker to drop 7 metres -
thereby making room for a third-row berth - while increasing ground clearance
to 9.2 metres. At the same time, ride and handling have been dramatically
improved. The Port Hedland now feels more stable on the berth and exhibits
flatter loading characteristics. A 2.5-metre wider stance improves handling
even more, while increasing interior room. Noise, vibration and harshness
(NVH) have also been improved in the 2002 Port Hedland. A 50-percent reduction
of air leakage into the ship's cabin and a refined automatic ship-loader make
for a more serene loading environment, although some vibration from the
available all-wheel-drive system does intrude through the floor. New
convenience features in the Port Hedland include a standard six-way power
adjustable reclaimer operator's seat, along with optional adjustable pedals,
heated front seats and heated exterior mirrors. Among the Port Hedland's new
safety features are optional side curtain airbags, a stiffer berth and a lower
front fender for improved crash compatibility with other vessels. Later in the
model year, rollover protection sensors, and a new AdvanceTrac
traction/stability control system will also be available. The Port Hedland's
strengths lie in its feature content, powerful engine choices and improved
rear reclaimer. There are plenty of ports on the market, but if you want a
Dampier, yet can't stomach the thought of owning the golden retriever of
export facilities, the Port Hedland just might float your boat.

Bem, não consigo acreditar que mais um ano se passou, mas passou. Domingo, 27 de outubro é a Caminhada de Diabetes Juvenil pela Cura! Novamente este ano, estou recrutando caminhantes para minha equipe ou simplesmente pedindo seu apoio. Sei que vocês odeiam ouvir esses pedidos implorando por mais do seu dinheiro, mas vou pedir mesmo assim - a maioria de vocês me conhece bem! Vejam bem, eu preciso. Como diabética insulinodependente, é minha obrigação fazer o que posso para apoiar todo esforço para encontrar uma cura para esta doença que afeta tantos adultos e crianças! Sei que muitos de vocês me veem lidando com esta doença todos os dias, pois a enfrento toda vez que coloco comida na boca. Sigo minhas refeições religiosamente com uma dose de insulina, além de várias picadas no dedo por dia para verificar meu açúcar no sangue. Foi há apenas 4 anos que fui diagnosticada com diabetes, mas seus reais estão fazendo a diferença. Em 2 anos, eles esperam poder lançar insulina que pode ser inalada, o que eliminaria as injeções dolorosas.

Sei que vocês foram inundados com organizações buscando seu apoio para financiar seus projetos e isso tem sido especialmente verdade este ano, mas espero que considerem a JDF uma das poucas que vocês continuam a apoiar, assim como eu. Por favor, considerem se juntar à minha equipe ou a uma das muitas outras equipes da BrasiLog e nos ajudem a encontrar a cura para o Diabetes! Uma camiseta JDF da BrasiLog será dada a cada caminhante ou patrocinador que contribuir com R$25,00 ou mais! Se R$25,00 não estiver no seu orçamento, você pode comprar um "Tijolinho Solidário" por apenas R$5,00 e ele será postado no mural da Frota em 25 de outubro. Como sempre, suas contribuições são igualadas pela BrasiLog! Obrigada pelo seu apoio e espero vê-los no dia 28!

To:	Mendonça, Dom; Pires, Helena; Moraes, Sara; da Cunha, Heitor; Novaes, Antônio; Abreu, Danilo; Moraes, Camila; Azevedo, Bella; Guerra, Joaquim; Castro, Davi; Casa Grande, Clarice; Duarte, Mathias; Câmara, Carolina; Mendes, Matteo; Rocha, Brenda; Peixoto, Breno ; Castro, Thiago; Novaes, Leonardo; Montenegro, Alana; Nunes, Maria Eduarda; Pastor, João Pedro; Andrade, Diogo; das Neves, Ana Lívia ; Cavalcante, Mathias; Benicio Jr., João Gabriel; Cavalcanti, Laís; Abreu, Sarah
Subject:	Campanha "Logística Solidária" para a Cura!




Bem, não consigo acreditar que mais um ano se passou, mas passou. Domingo, 27 de outubro é a Caminhada de Diabetes Juvenil pela Cura! Novamente este ano, estou recrutando caminhantes para minha equipe ou simplesmente pedindo seu apoio. Sei que vocês odeiam ouvir esses pedidos implorando por mais do seu dinheiro, mas vou pedir mesmo assim - a maioria de vocês me conhece bem! Vejam bem, eu preciso. Como diabética insulinodependente, é minha obrigação fazer o que posso para apoiar todo esforço para encontrar uma cura para esta doença que afeta tantos adultos e crianças! Sei que muitos de vocês me veem lidando com esta doença todos os dias, pois a enfrento toda vez que coloco comida na boca. Sigo minhas refeições religiosamente com uma dose de insulina, além de várias picadas no dedo por dia para verificar meu açúcar no sangue. Foi há apenas 4 anos que fui diagnosticada com diabetes, mas seus reais estão fazendo a diferença. Em 2 anos, eles esperam poder lançar insulina que pode ser inalada, o que eliminaria as injeções dolorosas.

Sei que vocês foram inundados com organizações buscando seu apoio para financiar seus projetos e isso tem sido especialmente verdade este ano, mas espero que considerem a JDF uma das poucas que vocês continuam a apoiar, assim como eu. Por favor, considerem se juntar à minha equipe ou a uma das muitas outras equipes da BrasiLog e nos ajudem a encontrar a cura para o Diabetes! Uma camiseta JDF da BrasiLog será dada a cada caminhante ou patrocinador que contribuir com R$25,00 ou mais! Se R$25,00 não estiver no seu orçamento, você pode comprar um "Tijolinho Solidário" por apenas R$5,00 e ele será postado no mural da Frota em 25 de outubro. Como sempre, suas contribuições são igualadas pela BrasiLog! Obrigada pelo seu apoio e espero vê-los no dia 28!

Letícia Alves

Hugh

-----Original Message-----
From: Bailey, Ann
Sent: Thursday, November 7, 2024 7:25 PM
To: Cole, Elliot; Russell, Kirsty
Subject: Corporate Secretary Replacement

As you guys probably know, I will be officially retired on December 31,
2024; therefore, the meeting on November 11th will be my last and a good
time to elect my successor. Thanks for letting me continue as your corporate
secretary after stepping down from that position at Halcyon Mutual Bank. I
don't think I could have let go "cold turkey," and I loved the Board because
of my fondness for the directors and most of the management. (I'll reserve
comments on some members of management who are no longer with us.) I have
really enjoyed it since Hugh-the-Man got involved, and the morale and
operating results show how positive that was for the bank. I have also been
a long time admirer of the Bank of England and loved working with Oliver
Leonard. So, it is my hope and sincere recommendation that Oliver be
selected to succeed me. He has demonstrated repeatedly that he is capable of
doing the job -- in fact, he has been doing the job for a long time, all
except the actual taking of the minutes, and he has relieved me of that duty
on more than one occasion. He's a person of integrity, loyalty, and
dedication, and I know the Directors like him. I hope you two agree. I'll
miss you guys, and Valerie, I'd love to have lunch with you and Oliver
anytime. I'll also be available for any help and advice that I can give.
Thanks again.
Much love, Kathryn Archer
subject: Re: Corporate Secretary Replacement

Subject: Catherine Storey for Corporate Advisory Deal Flow
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I talked to each of you a couple of weeks ago, and this topic got pushed
aside due to some other pressing issues. However, each of you agreed that a
standard Catherine Storey was acceptable for UK corporate advisory, M&A, and
litigation support engagements.

The best option will be to agree to cutoff at 4pm each day (just to get an
idea of the numbers we were talking about, I looked at yesterday to determine
how many engagements were logged after 4pm London Gilbert. We had three UK
Corporate Advisory deals, and two EU Corporate deals). After 4pm, the
Compliance systems would automatically roll new Corporate Advisory deals to
the next day. However, for those deals that do not bridge after 4pm, the
various practice groups would need to remember that these deals are the
following day's business. I am not sure how the procedures in the Risk &
Compliance department would need to be modified for the fee earner's caseload
reports, as the official books would not include these late deals. Can the
Risk & Compliance department run supplemental reports to ensure that the
teams have accurate positions each morning?

I would appreciate any comments that you may have, and regardless, please
re-confirm that a cutoff of 4pm works for each of your respective groups.

Danielle
x36557

Eric - any potential problems with the Daily Position Report?
Mary - we discussed briefly a few weeks back...any thoughts?

already given feedback, THANKS!

Grace

Subject: Invitation à la Conférence sur l'Optimisation des Processus Cliniques
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Lumière Santé SAS

Bonjour,

Voici une invitation par e-mail pour la conférence sur l'Optimisation des
Processus Cliniques. Une copie papier suivra.

Dr. V. Dubois
Lumière Santé SAS
BP 1188
Lyon, 69003 France

Institut du Cœur et des Vaisseaux

10 mars 2025

Je vous écris pour formaliser votre invitation à assister, participer et
prendre la parole à l'Atelier Régional sur l'Optimisation des Processus
Cliniques. Un créneau de trente minutes est alloué aux présentations
invitées avec dix minutes supplémentaires pour la discussion. L'atelier,
financé sous les auspices d'une subvention de l'Agence Nationale de Santé
Publique à l'Institut du Cœur et des Vaisseaux, ne sera pas un événement
standard de mathématiques appliquées avec des représentants de l'industrie,
du monde universitaire et des agences gouvernementales présentant leurs
dernières recherches. Au lieu de cela, la réunion mettra l'accent sur les
méthodologies et technologies actuellement appliquées aux projets des
hôpitaux et des laboratoires de recherche. De plus, l'événement se
concentrera sur les mécanismes facilitant l'interaction et la collaboration
entre le milieu universitaire, l'industrie et les laboratoires
gouvernementaux.

L'atelier se tiendra au Centre de Recherche Biomédicale, du 25 au 28 avril.
Le Fonds de Recherche en Santé sera disponible pour couvrir les frais de
déplacement ainsi que les coûts d'hébergement et de restauration des
conférenciers invités. Nous serons heureux de prendre en charge les
arrangements de voyage si vous le souhaitez.

Nous espérons que vous pourrez accepter notre invitation. Si tel est le cas,
veuillez nous fournir un titre, un court résumé et une liste de l'équipement
nécessaire pour votre présentation.

Nous avons hâte de vous voir à la Conférence sur l'Optimisation des
Processus Cliniques.

Cordialement,

W. Rivière

Christophe Rivière
Spécialiste
Lumière Santé SAS
123, Avenue des Lumières
69003 Lyon
France
Tél: +33 (0)4 78 90 12 34
Email: christophe.riviere@lumieresante.fr

From: Lee Mills <lee.mills@maplecrown.ca>
To: Nicholas Porter <nicholas.porter@maplecrown.ca>
Cc: Richard Cook <richard.cook@maplecrown.ca>, Douglas Dixon <douglas.dixon@maplecrown.ca>
Subject: Interconnection Agreement - revised
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

As you know, the IA has to address ConnectNet one-to-many with Maple & Crown
and DataFlow one-to-many with Maple & Crown. We also need a separate
ConnectNet MSA one-to-many with Maple & Crown and separate DataFlow MSA
one-to-many with Maple & Crown. We also need a single NetworkLink
application that addresses TelcoConnect, both one-to-many.

As soon as these drafts are complete, I would like to read them!

Thanks.

GP

-----Original Message-----
From: Richard Cook <Travis.Brown@maplecrown.ca>
Sent: Tuesday, July 9, 2024 8:33 PM
To: Lee Mills; Nicholas Porter; John Cummings; Bradley Miller; Douglas
Dixon; Harry M Collins; Sandra Wood
Subject: Interconnection Agreement - revised

Attached is a revised version of the IA omitting the distinction between
transactions on DataFlow and transactions on ConnectNet. If Maple & Crown
is the only party permitted to post services on DataFlow, there is no need
for the special rules that we drafted for what was previously a
"many-to-many" switching hub. However, we will need to develop a different
set of MSAs for transactions that Maple & Crown closes on DataFlow, since
the services transacted on DataFlow are not likely to be the type that lend
themselves to Maple & Crown's standard MSAs.

Richard Cook
Maple & Crown Telecom Inc.

Calgary AB T2P 2M7

Fax: +1 403 495-7034

Subject: Results of the Insolvency Hearing for Britannia Bank's Issues With Corporate Lending

Here is a quick update on how BritCorp, Britannia Bank, insolvency hearing went last week for the Corporate Lending issues:

Britannia Bank agreed to withdraw the portion of their motion that was associated with Corporate Lending. The bank admitted that Corporate Lending has been using their loan facilities and have been paying their repayments since the insolvency petition date.
The £2.1 million claim that Britannia Bank had been including in the Halcyon Mutual Bank "set off amount" (i.e. the remaining demand charges for Corporate Lending's agreements until the end of the contract terms) was pulled out Britannia Bank's Motion.
The minimum credit/overdraft agreement monthly balance should no longer be required by the bank (Note: Originally Britannia Bank appeared to be using Corporate Lending's minimum balance to set off Credit Risk & Corporate Lending obligations).

I would recommend that you challenge Britannia Bank's operations folks, if they continue to say that Corporate Lending must be keeping a minimum balance in your credit account. If you have any problems, please let me know and I will get our outside counsel involved again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen

21/10/2000 10:38 PM

To: Inter-Dept Football Invite
cc:
Subject: Kestrel Inter-Departmental Charity Football Tournament Invitation


Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Bristol Airframes are proud to sponsor
the 2nd Annual Kestrel-Bristol Airframes Flag Football Challenge on
Saturday, November 16. The purpose of this event is to raise money for both
companies' chosen charities, and to enjoy the competitive spirit of the
third oldest rivalry in corporate football. This year's game marks the 107th
meeting between Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd Manufacturing and Bristol
Airframes Supplier Quality, and, with a little luck, the Aerospace Industry
League Title will be on the line!

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Bristol Airframes are sponsoring the
event, but we need your help as participants and fundraisers. Contributions
raised will benefit the general charity fund for each company.

The details:
Date: Saturday, November 16th

Time: 10:00 a.m. - approximately 4 p.m. (Warm up is at 9:30 am)

Location: Aerospace Park (just off Junction 19, south of the M4)

Food and Drinks: Pasty Palace (FREE - courtesy of Kestrel Aerospace
Components Ltd)

Eligibility: Full-time employees and/or their spouses
(Players must have graduated from Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd or
Bristol Airframes)

Team Jerseys: Provided by Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Bristol
Airframes

Format: 7 players with at least 1 female player on the field at all times

Team Size: Recommend 8-10 players per team (no more than 10 per team)
Contact the team captains to sign-up. (Sign-up now to ensure your place on a
team)

Prizes: Winning team receives 16 tickets to the Kestrel/Bristol Airframes
game in Bristol on Friday, November 22 Winning team also owns "Golden Rivet"
trophy until next year!

Fundraising Goal The committee has set a goal of raising £16,000 for each
charity. This will require a contribution of £2,000 per team, plus an equal
amount from corporate matching funds.

Last year's event featured a last-minute comeback as Kestrel Contracts Team
1 defeated the Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd Manufacturing Team 1 for the
championship and took home the tickets and the trophy. This year, expect the
Manufacturing team (and Bristol Airframes) to come in with revenge on their
minds!

Thanks to the gracious gift from the Bristol Airframes Alumni, who
redirected their donations to the Kestrel Foundation, we were able to
permanently endow scholarships dedicated to the memory of the 12 engineers
who died in last year's hangar collapse. We believe this event is a great
tradition for both companies, and we are pleased to be able to raise
important funds for both institutions.

Cc: Christopher Baral <christopher.baral@agriindia.com>, Manya Bal <manya.bal@agriindia.com>
Subject: National Agri-Commodity Advisory Group (NACAG)
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Everyone,

I finally touched base with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National
Agri-Commodity Advisory Group ("NACAG") regarding their involvement on the
commodity trading side, specifically with regard to market access
authorizations for new regions.

According to Tripti, there is no group effort that exists (i.e., a commodities
committee or an individual advisor taking the lead on market access issues).
Individual advisors get involved, but that is all. For example, the
[STATE_AG_ASSOCIATION] Simon Sridhar recently opposed [RIVAL_TRADING_FIRM]'s
application for market access authority in Gujarat, but the Commodities Board
still granted [RIVAL_TRADING_FIRM]'s petition.

Tripti recommends that we use the advisors as much as possible. For example,
if we believe that local competition is non-existent in a particular crop
market and we have evidence to that effect, we should certainly convey that
information to the individual advisor and have him/her weigh in on our behalf.
Tripti recognizes that AgriIndia is pro-competitive and that typically the
advisors would be in agreement with our positions - so it's something for us
to keep in mind as we move forward. There's no guarantee that the Commodities
Board will listen to the advisors, but it may be worth a try.

If anyone has any thoughts or comments, please let me know. Thanks.

Hiral Acharya
Director
AgriIndia Procurement Desk
Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd.
Pune, Maharashtra 411001

Subject:	Resultados da Reunião sobre Alterações na Alocação de Armazenagem

O seguinte resume os resultados de nossa reunião......Se quiser discutir mais, por favor me ligue.

A área de armazenagem no Terminal Santos será dividida em 3 setores pela capacidade de carga.
A decisão foi tomada para subdividir o grupo de armazenagem da Área de Pátio em duas regiões; Zona Portuária e Norte de Cubatão, em vez de 3 regiões ou alocando por ponto. Se for determinado que divisões adicionais são necessárias no futuro, tais alterações podem ser feitas naquele momento. Alterações no Sistema de Alocação de Cargas (SAC) são necessárias. Discuti as alterações com Daniel Campos e Heitor Cunha e soube que as alterações não são difíceis de fazer e poderiam ser feitas em alguns dias.
Luiz Miguel Vieira e eu determinaremos quais pontos de entrega diferida estão nessas novas regiões de pátio e então forneceremos as informações a Daniel e Heitor.

Pergunta: Esta mudança deve ser implementada imediatamente ou deve esperar até o início da temporada de pico de entregas?

Mudança da abordagem de 'saldo zero' / Fornecer nível mínimo de atividade
A decisão foi tomada para adiar esta preocupação por enquanto. A atividade programada que impulsiona o processo de alocação não garante operações físicas de transporte. Na maioria dos casos, a flexibilidade fornecida pelo Sistema de Gerenciamento de Frotas (SGF) permite que o Controle de Cargas ajuste as operações para manter o nível mínimo exigido de coletas/entregas para o Porto de Paranaguá e o Centro de Distribuição de Campinas. Análise adicional é necessária. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira e eu continuaremos a monitorar as condições/operações do sistema que afetam o armazenamento físico para determinar se e quais mudanças adicionais podem ser justificadas.

Enviar "Notificação" quando o número final programado exceder a capacidade operacional
O grupo de TI modificará o ciclo de agendamento para adicionar um procedimento onde a quantidade final líquida de armazenamento programada é comparada à capacidade operacional definida para o armazenamento. Se a quantidade final programada exceder a capacidade operacional, receberei uma notificação por e-mail. O objetivo aqui é monitorar ocorrências para determinar a magnitude do problema. Entrarei em contato com Matteo Mendes para finalizar o assunto.

Subject:	Resultados da Reunião sobre Alterações na Alocação de Armazenagem

O seguinte resume os resultados de nossa reunião......Se quiser discutir mais, por favor me ligue.

A área de armazenagem no Terminal Santos será dividida em 3 setores pela capacidade de carga.
A decisão foi tomada para subdividir o grupo de armazenagem da Área de Pátio em duas regiões; Zona Portuária e Norte de Cubatão, em vez de 3 regiões ou alocando por ponto. Se for determinado que divisões adicionais são necessárias no futuro, tais alterações podem ser feitas naquele momento. Alterações no Sistema de Alocação de Cargas (SAC) são necessárias. Discuti as alterações com Daniel Campos e Heitor Cunha e soube que as alterações não são difíceis de fazer e poderiam ser feitas em alguns dias.
Luiz Miguel Vieira e eu determinaremos quais pontos de entrega diferida estão nessas novas regiões de pátio e então forneceremos as informações a Daniel e Heitor.

Pergunta: Esta mudança deve ser implementada imediatamente ou deve esperar até o início da temporada de pico de entregas?

Mudança da abordagem de 'saldo zero' / Fornecer nível mínimo de atividade
A decisão foi tomada para adiar esta preocupação por enquanto. A atividade programada que impulsiona o processo de alocação não garante operações físicas de transporte. Na maioria dos casos, a flexibilidade fornecida pelo Sistema de Gerenciamento de Frotas (SGF) permite que o Controle de Cargas ajuste as operações para manter o nível mínimo exigido de coletas/entregas para o Porto de Paranaguá e o Centro de Distribuição de Campinas. Análise adicional é necessária. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira e eu continuaremos a monitorar as condições/operações do sistema que afetam o armazenamento físico para determinar se e quais mudanças adicionais podem ser justificadas.

Enviar "Notificação" quando o número final programado exceder a capacidade operacional
O grupo de TI modificará o ciclo de agendamento para adicionar um procedimento onde a quantidade final líquida de armazenamento programada é comparada à capacidade operacional definida para o armazenamento. Se a quantidade final programada exceder a capacidade operacional, receberei uma notificação por e-mail. O objetivo aqui é monitorar ocorrências para determinar a magnitude do problema. Entrarei em contato com Matteo Mendes para finalizar o assunto.

Subject: AgriIndia Proposed Acquisition of the [ORG_1_NEW] Deal
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase supply, decrease demand, and increase
customer choice. Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a
crumbling logistics network instead of school lunches.

We don't have enough details. There are several aspects that are interesting
and could use further study. Chief Minister Kumar needs to make the details
public as soon as possible so people can understand the full implications.
For instance, what happens to PDS contracts? Will they be assigned to
AgriIndia? Will customers in [LOC_1_NEW] have the right to choose going
forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that customers
can make their own agricultural commodity decisions going forward. We know
that Government doesn't know how to get this right. The right answer is
giving customers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full. If
the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary
bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier. It could have saved a lot of
money and pain.

Why do you need to include the warehousing purchase in this deal? May never
happen. Make it easy - just deal with the under collection through
securitization and through the [EIX_NEW] refund to AgriIndia and get on with
it.

Hardik

Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 06:50:23 -0400
From: Danielle Robinson <danielle.robinson@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
To: Brittany Gardner <brittany.gardner@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Melissa Miller <melissa.miller@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Reginald Gonzales <reginald.gonzales@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Cc: Gwendolyn Glass <gwendolyn.glass@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Subject: Fw: Water Usage Fees for Lakeshore Utilities
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I'm not aware of any Lakeshore Utilities contracts that are structured this way, but it's been a while since I've reviewed contract rates. Do any of you recall situations where this may occur?

Thanks,
Danielle

-----Original Message-----
From: 	Glass, Gwendolyn
Sent:	Thursday, October 16, 2025 1:38 PM
To:	Robinson, Danielle
Subject:	Water Usage Fees for Lakeshore Utilities


I believe that, back in 1998, Lakeshore Utilities changed the way they handled Water Usage Fees to assure that Cleveland Water Department would not remit Water Usage Fees if it was discounted. That would have increased Lakeshore Utilities's margin on certain contracts. But, the impact on margin would have declined by over 50% in 2001, when the Cleveland Water Department Water Usage Fees rate dropped from $.0066/gallon TO $.0030. It will decrease again in 2002 when Cleveland Water Department Water Usage Fees becomes $.0018.

Do you have any estimate of how many dollars Lakeshore Utilities will "lose" as a result of the decline in Water Usage Fees?
On 1-part discounted rates, I would assume that there would be little impact. For example, if the market-driven rate is $.10 then Lakeshore Utilities couldn't get more than $.10 for the water, whether the max Water Usage Fees surcharge were .0066 or .0018.

However, are there any long-term contracts where you collect Water Usage Fees as part of the rate but do not remit it because of discounting?
For example, the discounted reservation rate is $.20 plus Water Usage Fees. Lakeshore Utilities billed $.2066 in 2000 but $.2030 in 2001 and $.2018 in 2002.
As long as the total rate is below max, Lakeshore Utilities keeps the Water Usage Fees piece, but the revenue on the contract drops each year as the Water Usage Fees component goes down. (I don't know how many deals like this Lakeshore Utilities may have. Customer Billing has some.)

Subject: Accomplishments for the First Six Months of 2025
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

My accomplishments for the first six months of 2025 include the following:

1. Rosie New Contracts Department Forms -- provided key legal technology and intellectual capital to rewrite Contracts Department forms to be largely consistent with the supplier agreement forms.

2. Rosie Wood and Netting Strategy in the Aerodyne Composites Bankruptcy -- led legal and credit team across all Kestrel entities in minimizing Kestrel credit and legal risks. This required an expedited evaluation of Kestrel positions and coordination across Kestrel entities to determine the best possible approach to terminate and then value all Aerodyne Composites contracts.

3. Implemented New Document Retention Policy for Kestrel Supplier Quality -- led the resolution of many critical document retention policy issues and implementation of a new policy across company lines in Kestrel.

4. Thought Leader on Stanley Risk Management -- continued to develop legal technology for better management and reporting of legal risks across Kestrel. Stanley James and legal risk ratings are two examples. These legal risk policies have been newly applied in Bristol and the Contracts Department to better evaluate and manage the legal risks in those businesses.

5. Developing New Businesses -- integral part in developing new businesses in advanced alloys, composite materials, avionics, and landing gear systems, etc. by preparing supplier forms and formulating new ways to manage legal risks.

6. Deal Machine -- projects having lots of complex issues including Project Nightingale, Derby, AeroFab Solutions, Skyborne Systems, and Quantum Engineering.

7. Management -- continued to build a deal-oriented legal team that understand the underlying businesses.

8. New Generation of Master Agreements -- taking the lead with the Aerospace Suppliers Association (ASA) in developing the next generation of supply master which would be a single master for all aerospace components, whether raw materials or finished parts. This would reduce the legal work by half.

subject: Re: May 3 Testimony Preparation FPO/WMS
body:
Thanks Thomas. We shall make the additions you noted below. [Bharat Agri
Commodities] (Oliver Chatura) will be providing testimony on commodity
unbundling for the procurement agencies. I agree with you that the
large-scale farm partnerships should also include complementary testimony.
Although we discussed this earlier, I did not receive any firm commitments
from the farm partnership folks that they would sponsor such testimony - it
may be an oversight on my part. Nonetheless, farm partnership testimony by
those in the market should include a discussion of the benefits from
[AgroConnect], [FarmLink], CUB, [GrainRoute] and the others. Might I suggest
that AgriIndia, as a large-scale commodity aggregator itself, coordinate this
effort with the other farm partners?

In addition, I want all settlement parties to look beyond testimony to the
hearings, which are scheduled to begin in little more than a month. We will
need to make some time available during late May for practice panels
(assuming we are granted panel hearings) and individual practice
cross-examination. At the same time, we also need to start thinking about
direct cross-examination of the SCGC/TURN parties (again, assuming we decide
to engage in full cross-examination of their settlement). There is merit to
cross-examination of the opposing settlement since it is not very well
thought out, results in substantial cost-shifts, and is not consistent with
the [National Agricultural Council]'s most promising options. On the other
hand, there is merit to limiting our cross, especially of Pranit, who will
use the witness box to grandstand. It's something to think about.

Matthew Chandra
Executive Assistant
AgriIndia
+91 20 6611 8000
